newsitem.title: USA: US manufacturers see productivity offsetting wages.
newsitem.headline: US manufacturers see productivity offsetting wages.

text.p: Most U.S. manufacturers foresee industrial productivity rising so briskly that it will offset wage increases this year, the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) said on Thursday.
Fully 89 percent of NAM directors said in a survey that they thought labor costs would remain stable in the year ahead because businesses would increase their production efficiency.
About 70 directors responded to the survey.

The finding was notable because the potential for increased wages has been widely cited as a reason for Federal Reserve policymakers' decision to raise short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point on March 25.
Private analysts said on Wednesday the concern was likely to be revived by a report of strong gains in March industrial production that pushed capacity use rates to a two-year high.
The Fed said that industrial output rose 0.9 percent last month and that the capacity use rate climbed to 84.1 percent -- highest since 84.3 percent in March 1995.

The NAM directors were universally opposed to more interest-rate hikes by the Fed. The survey found 59 percent of respondents felt that rates should be held where they were while the remaining 41 percent favored lower rates.
An overwhelming 91 percent of the NAM directors said they saw no significant signs of economic "overheating" in either price or labor markets.
Most seemed to feel the rate of economic growth would ease moderately in the final six months this year.

While a combined 82 percent foresaw gross domestic product expanding at an annual rate of between two percent and three percent in the first half, 50 percent said growth would be between two percent and 2.5 percent in the second half.

And while only four percent predicted first-half growth under two percent, a much larger 24 percent of respondents said they thought GDP would expand by less than two percent in the closing six months of this year.
